statement: Let T5 have the ten 2-subsets of {0,1,2,3,4} as vertices, with distinct vertices adjacent iff they intersect. Define M_n=alpha(T5 strong power n) and Theta(T5)=sup_n M_n^(1/n). Determine Theta(T5).
goals: Prove Theta(T5)=5/2 or determine its actual value; do not presuppose either endpoint.
Separate milestone: exhibit 63 pairwise distinguishable length-five words to refute Theta(T5)=12^(1/3), since 63^3>12^5.
prior_notes: Earlier work reports 2,5,12,27 for M_1..M_4 and a 60-word length-five code, plus a 5/2 upper bound. These are leads requiring independent source or certificate validation. Reported unsuccessful directions include fixed-type codes, local repairs, translation symmetry and fractional Haemers improvements; inspect before treating as excluded. Earlier conversations also propose competing endpoint hypotheses; neither is assumed.
routes: finite combinatorial construction / SAT / maximum clique
upper bounds via asymptotic spectrum / nonmultiplicative certificates
literature transfer from zero-error information theory
counterexample to proposed lemmas or endpoints
